title: AC1024 TABLE body-string cursor reconciliation
scope: Reconcile the specified ODA detached-TV path against a diagnostic body-byte-counted string hypothesis on two TABLE records in the existing hash-bound AC1024 candidate. This receipt records the completed local raw-retention compatibility slice and its bounded controls; it does not select a semantic wire profile or qualify TABLE output.

authority.primary: ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1 §§20.4.96.2, 20.4.97, and 20.4.99
authority.specifiedProfile: For AC1024, TABLECONTENT is embedded in ACAD_TABLE; a type-4 CadValue string uses TV, with R2007+ text in the detached string stream.
authority.conflict: The diagnostic body-byte-counted string hypothesis aligns the observed candidate cursors but conflicts with the specified type-4 detached-TV layout. ODA remains authoritative until an erratum or independent source-bound explanation resolves the conflict.

result: The local AC1024 TABLE raw-retention slice is implemented and its seven focused generated-vector selectors pass. The source-bound ACadSharp sample reaches the bounded fallback for TABLE handles 0x528 and 0xa35, leaving respectively 3 and 7 untyped handle-stream bits. Paired DXFs match selected text, but ODA v5.4.1 §20.4.99 specifies detached TV for type-4 CadValue strings and remains authoritative. No cell semantics are published, strict output remains refused, and the separate OBJECTCONTEXTDATA blocker prevents whole-file conversion. This closes only the local reader sub-slice; producer-bound field/role evidence, graph closure, strict output, independent readback, and native appearance remain open. No fixture was added.

sampleRun.result: Both bounded AC1024 body-string candidates reached raw-only retention; no cell or table-style semantics were published. The whole-file conversion refused before output because standalone OBJECTCONTEXTDATA has no qualified replay path; the destination DXF was not created.

implementationRun.tailDisposition: The detached string cursor accepts only zero footer/alignment bits within its 14-bit bound. The handle cursor may retain at most seven remaining bits as opaque source-frame data; the observed candidates leave 3 and 7 bits. These bits are not labeled padding or assigned semantics. This exception is safe only on the raw-retaining, semantic-incomplete path, which remains refused by strict output.
